To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified a de novo loss-of function mutation in the GRN2A/Glu2A gene in patients with childhood focal epilepsy, which decreases the function of NMDARs.

the GluA(D731N)/GluN2A(D732N) mutation decreases NMDAR function, and the mutant decreases NMDA potency by over 3000-fold, reduces current response amplitude and channel open probability, and enhances sensitivity to proton inhibition.

a de novo missence GRIN2A (GluN2A) mutation (D731N) was found in a child with epilepsy and ID, and that this mutation decreases NMDA receptor function, suggesting NMDA hypofunction may play a role in epilepsy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a GRIN2 gene mutation that causes a severe form of epilepsy.
the genetic and electrophysiological characterization of a de novo loss of function GRIN2A variant in a child with epilepsy, developmental delay, and acquired epilepticaphasia.
a new mutation in GRIN2A that may contribute to childhood epilepsy and ID/DD, and may have important implications for the understanding of the pathogenesis of NMDAR hypotunction in epilepsy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GRIN2 mutation is a de novo loss-of function mutation that causes a decrease in glutamate binding, a decrease in current amplitude and a decrease in channel open probability.
the Glu N2A mutation identified here causes a loss of function of NMDA receptors.
the GRIN2 mutation identified in the patient in this report is a de novo loss-of- function GRIN2A (GluN2A) mutation associated with childhood acquired epileptic aphasi and focal epilepsy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a de novo GRIN2A (GluN2A) mutation in a child with epilepsy and ID.

the Glu(D731N) mutant decreases NMDA receptor function by reducing the potency and efficacy of the agonist, increasing sensitivity to negative allostersic modulators, and reducing the channel open probability.
a de novo missence GRIN2A(D731) mutation in a patient with unexplained epilepsy causes a decrease in NMDAR activation and function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GRIN2A mutations can cause a spectrum of epilepsy phenotypes.
the Glu2A(D731)N mutation is a loss-of-function mutation that causes NMDAR hypotfunction.
NMDA receptor dysfunction can cause epilepsy, and that NMDA hypofunction is a potential mechanism for acquired epileptic aphaisa.
